meta.title: Hive: from browser task to CLI worker
meta.subtitle: Local team path · terminal bytes are live visibility; team messages and reports are structured collaboration

components.label: Workbench terminals
components.sublabel: Enter a goal; watch CLI output
components.explanation: The browser connects per run to /ws/terminal/:runId/io and /control. Input reaches the CLI through the server PTY, not a browser-side agent. The orchestrator terminal is the interactive entry shown here; worker terminals use the same transport.

components.label: PTY runtime + stream hub
components.sublabel: Spawn, write, mirror and fan out
components.explanation: Hive starts configured CLIs through node-pty. Terminal input is written to the run; PTY onData publishes to the output bus and the stream hub fans it out to viewers. Dispatch/report envelopes also use the runtime's CLI-aware input writer. Both server boxes in this drawing belong to the same Hive runtime, not separate services.

components.label: Orchestrator CLI
components.explanation: The orchestrator invokes the local team CLI: team send <member> <task>. That helper posts to 127.0.0.1:HIVE_PORT with project identity and an agent token. Agent behavior is prompted, not guaranteed: Hive does not deterministically turn every natural-language goal into a dispatch.

components.label: Team / Action Center
components.explanation: The Action Center polls the UI API every two seconds, with UI-token authentication on the server. Its summary is built from team state, dispatches and messages; this is separate from streaming terminal output.

components.label: Worker CLI
components.explanation: A configured worker receives a dispatch envelope through its PTY. For structured progress it runs team message --dispatch <id> --to orchestrator --kind progress. It ends a responsibility with team report --dispatch <id> and optional artifact paths. Printing terminal output alone is not a team report.

components.label: Team API + collaboration
components.explanation: CLI requests are authenticated and role-gated. Dispatches are recorded before a formatted prompt is written through the agent runtime. User-managed stopped workers remain queued until started; the first send can wake a never-started orchestrator-spawned worker. Reports close the matching open dispatch and enqueue an orchestrator envelope before delivery. Completion recording is distinct from delivery to the orchestrator.

sources.label: Auth, role check and stopped-worker policy
Create, queue, claim and write dispatch

components.label: Local runtime.sqlite
components.explanation: The local runtime database stores dispatch lifecycle, report text and artifact path references. Dispatch messages and report envelopes have outboxes so recording does not depend on an active recipient PTY. These are local SQLite records, not an external queue service. Artifact paths are references, not evidence of an uploaded artifact store.

cards.title: Two return channels
items: Live: PTY bytes → output bus → WebSocket terminals.
Structured: progress messages / final report → team state + orchestrator PTY.

cards.title: Lifecycle and delivery gates
items: Stopped user-managed worker: queue, then replay on start.
Report recorded ≠ delivered. Offline orchestrator leaves an outbox backlog; team list retries it.

cards.title: Scope and limits
items: Local team path; both Hive server boxes are one runtime. Remote relay and optional workflows omitted.
.hive/tasks.md is a separate task document, not an automatic dispatch queue. Agent command compliance is not guaranteed.
